vlog_arc.theme: Consistency is the product — showing up when the system is still being built

beats.mon: Leo opens the week at 5am, formula in hand, and says directly to camera: this week I'm not chasing a viral moment — I'm proving that the system works when I show up anyway.
beats.tue: Leo shares one operational gap from last week that suppressed reach, names exactly what broke, and explains the fix he put in place this morning before the kids woke up.
beats.wed: Leo films himself reviewing a real customer message — reads it aloud, pauses, and talks about what it means to build something that actually changes someone's afternoon.
beats.thu: Leo walks through the ingredient shortlist decision for the next formula iteration — not a pitch, just a founder thinking out loud about why he cut one adaptogen he loved.
beats.fri: Leo closes his laptop at 4pm, picks up Gabriel and Helena, and tells camera: the goal was to be present at 4pm — the formula and the system both have to earn that.
beats.sat: Leo films a quiet Saturday morning training session, no music, no voiceover cuts, just him moving and then sitting down with a cup — letting the routine speak for itself.
beats.sun: Leo looks at next week's plan, names the one thing he is most uncertain about, and says: I'm publishing it anyway — building in public means the uncertainty ships too.

ig.title: Your 3pm slump isn't laziness
ig.angle: Hook: you blame yourself every afternoon — payoff: reveal it's a blood-sugar architecture problem that functional coffee addresses before noon.

ig.title: Day 1 skeptic. Day 7 convert.
ig.angle: Mirror the buyer's resistance arc beat by beat — skepticism on day one is validated, then resolved by day seven with a real customer quote and timestamp.

ig.title: Two hours before the world wakes
ig.angle: Leo's 5am window — Ironman training, formula in hand, kids still asleep — shows what sustainable output actually looks like before the workday starts.

ig.title: Why functional coffee beats a stack
ig.angle: Frame Power Coffee against the four-supplement morning ritual: same cognitive targets, one cup, a fraction of the cost per day — let the math close it.

ig.title: The tree that survived a nuclear blast
ig.angle: Lead with the Ginkgo biloba Hiroshima survival claim, hold the ingredient name until slide two, then connect its mechanism to the 11am fog your reader feels right now.

x.title: Energy drinks sell volts. We sell clarity.
x.angle: One sharp declarative that separates stimulant-spike culture from sustained cognitive output — positions Power Coffee without naming a competitor.

x.title: The functional coffee ingredient decision framework
x.angle: A five-point thread Leo uses internally to decide which adaptogens earn a place in the formula — teaches the audience how to read any product label.

x.title: I built this for the dad at hour ten
x.angle: Declarative confession: Leo was losing the evening with his kids because caffeine crashed him by 4pm — the formula was a parenting solution before it was a product.

x.title: $0.73 a morning. Real focus. No crash.
x.angle: Price-math post that dismantles the premium objection by putting it next to the daily latte spend and a concrete cognitive output claim.

x.title: More caffeine is not the answer
x.angle: Reframe the cultural default — the crash is not a dosage problem, it's an ingredient architecture problem — and let the tension do the selling.

li.title: I spent two years getting this wrong
li.angle: Leo narrates the formulation failure arc — the blends that didn't work, what he learned from each iteration — because founder-narrated ingredient science drives 2x engagement on LinkedIn.

li.title: How to read a functional coffee label
li.angle: A practical framework post — five questions every founder or exec should ask before choosing a functional product — positions Leo as the category educator, not just a seller.

li.title: The supplement stack is a UX problem
li.angle: Reframe for the LinkedIn professional: managing five morning capsules is friction that compounds over time — one functional cup is a systems decision, not a health trend.

li.title: A review stopped me mid-scroll
li.angle: Open with a verbatim customer moment, unpack what specifically shifted for that buyer on day three, and connect it to the formulation decision that made it possible.

li.title: Why I co-created this formula with AI
li.angle: Radical transparency post — Leo names the AI-assisted R&D process, refuses to apologize for it, and explains why it produced a more rigorous ingredient selection than traditional CPG.

tg.title: Behind the week: what didn't ship
tg.angle: Leo shares one thing that failed in operations this week and what the fix looks like — radical transparency with the inner circle builds trust that no ad copy can manufacture.

tg.title: This week's numbers, unfiltered
tg.angle: Raw weekly metrics — reach, engagement rate, conversion — shared with context so the community understands what growth actually looks like at this stage.

tg.title: Why I stopped optimizing copy first
tg.angle: Structural insight: consistent publishing outperforms brilliant copy when the pipeline has gaps — the lesson Leo is building the business around this quarter.

tg.title: The adaptogens shortlist: what made the cut
tg.angle: Inside-channel exclusive — Leo walks through the three adaptogens that almost made the formula and why each was cut, teaching ingredient evaluation in real time.

tg.title: 430 mornings. What I actually notice.
tg.angle: Specific, unmarketed personal data — the cognitive and physical patterns Leo has observed across 430 consecutive mornings with the formula, no claims, just observed patterns.

blog.title: Functional coffee vs energy drinks: a clear breakdown
blog.angle: A definitive, SEO-anchored comparison that teaches the mechanism differences — stimulant spike vs adaptive output — and lets the science make the argument for switching.

blog.title: Why Ginkgo biloba survived Hiroshima and your 11am
blog.angle: Lead with the historical survival claim, build to the neuroprotective mechanism, close with how it addresses the afternoon cognitive dip most professionals accept as normal.

blog.title: Blood sugar is running your mornings, not caffeine
blog.angle: Reframe post: the crash is not a caffeine withdrawal problem — it is a glycemic architecture problem — and functional ingredients are the structural fix, not more espresso.

blog.title: Building in public: Leo's formulation failure log
blog.angle: A candid narrative of the two-year formulation journey — the blends that failed, the pivot moments, the family stakes — showing the product as the output of real sacrifice.

blog.title: How to evaluate any functional coffee product
blog.angle: An evergreen buyer's framework — five criteria Leo uses — that educates the reader, builds category authority, and filters for the buyer who is ready for Power Coffee.

em.title: What I told my kids I was building

em.angle: Price-math email that walks through the daily cost comparison against lattes and supplement stacks, framing Power Coffee as the highest-ROI cognitive tool in a founder's morning.
